question: Why can consciousness be spoken of as both cause and effect?
premises: The consciousness of the lord of consciousness is nothing other than consciousness itself.
The terms effect and cause are applied to it.
This application is figurative rather than a real division.
inference: Because consciousness remains only consciousness, the distinction between cause and effect is applied to it only figuratively.
plain_english: The consciousness of the lord of consciousness would be consciousness alone; therefore, since it is spoken of as both effect and cause, that status is applied only figuratively.
